outcome: No compact or finite-volume example in any frozen prefix. The 2sqrt(2) seed is the most wall-rich early branch (27 accepted walls), but its sparse strict hyperideal witness survives through H=27; the sqrt(2) witness survives three further empty shells through H=40.

scope.claim: Three complete primitive chronological prefixes for the unit, sqrt(2), and 2sqrt(2) coefficients. Each has an explicit strict hyperideal ray. These are bounded screens, not global nonreflectivity theorems.
scope.spatial_lattice: Niemeier N(D12^2), exact vector-spinor graph glue {(0,0),(v,s),(s,v),(c,c)}

searches.complete_norm_class_proof: Put pi=sqrt(2) and epsilon=1+pi. The coefficient epsilon is a unit and N(D12^2) is even unimodular. For primitive r=(x,y), reflection integrality says q(r) divides 2I(r), I(r)=(epsilon*x,(y,N)). Away from (pi), local unimodularity and primitivity make I(r) the unit ideal. At (pi), a unit control gives v_pi(q)=0; otherwise a primitive spatial coordinate makes I(r) a unit, while evenness and q|2I force v_pi(q)=2. Every totally-positive unit of Z[sqrt(2)] is a square, so the complete canonical positive norms are 1 and 2.

Put pi=sqrt(2), so (2)=(pi)^2. For primitive r=(x,y), reflection integrality is q(r)|2I(r), I(r)=(pi*x,(y,N)). The spatial lattice N(D12^2) is even unimodular. Away from (pi), local unimodularity and primitivity make I(r) the unit ideal. If x is a unit then v_pi(q)=1; otherwise a primitive spatial coordinate is a unit and evenness plus q|2I gives v_pi(q)=2. Totally-positive units are squares, so the complete canonical norms are 2 and 2+pi.

Put pi=sqrt(2), so the coefficient 2sqrt(2)=pi^3. For primitive r=(x,y), q(r)|2I(r), I(r)=(pi^3*x,(y,N)), and N(D12^2) is even unimodular. If a spatial coordinate is a unit, evenness and q|2I give v_pi(q)=2. Otherwise x is a unit and y is pi-divisible, giving v_pi(q)=3. Totally-positive units are squares, so the complete canonical norms are 2 and 4+2pi.
